Rules:

- If your result matches none of the options, set "status" to "no_option_matches" and give your result in "value".
- A blank or missing option never matches. Do not guess what it was meant to say.
- If more than one option is correct in a single-correct question, or none is, say so in "note".
- Answer format:
  - single-correct: one letter, for example "B"
  - multiple-correct: every correct letter, comma separated, for example "A, C, D"

request.user:
Subject: Physics
Question type: multiple-correct (one or more options are right)

Which of the following are scalar quantities?
(A) Work
(B) Momentum
(C) Electric current
(D) Pressure

result.working: Work W = F·d is a dot product, so it is a scalar. Momentum p = mv has direction and adds as a vector, so it is a vector. Electric current has a sense of flow but does not obey vector addition (currents at a junction add algebraically), so it is a scalar. Pressure is normal force per unit area, it acts equally in all directions at a point and has no specific direction, so it is a scalar.
